overall: Atlanta reached a daily high of 91.4°F around 17:00 ET, surpassing all NWP model forecasts before a line of severe thunderstorms swept through and sharply dropped temperatures to 82.4°F by 20:00 ET. Active Severe Thunderstorm Warnings and a Severe Thunderstorm Watch through 11 PM EDT confirm ongoing convective activity across the metro area. The day started warm and humid with overcast skies, heated rapidly through the afternoon, then was disrupted by the storm passage, which appears to have definitively ended the warming phase.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models undershot the actual observed high — ECMWF at 87.5°F, NBM at 86.8°F, and even the warmest (HRRR at 90.1°F) fell short of the 91.4°F running max. The INTRADAY model concentrated 96.8% probability in the 90–91°F bucket, which closely brackets the observed peak, while the META model's mass in higher buckets (92–95°F range) is now clearly inconsistent with the observed temperature trajectory and the post-storm cool-down.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max locked at 91.4°F, temperatures currently at 82.4°F and falling, and multiple active severe thunderstorm warnings keeping skies cloudy and winds gusty, there is no realistic pathway for temperatures to recover and exceed 91.4°F before midnight. The give-up classifier firing at hour 14.67 (slightly premature, as the true peak came near 17:00 ET) and the sustained post-storm cool-down further cement this conclusion. Confidence is very high that today's official TMAX is 91.4°F.
